_about: Batch B10b writer: the Python and C++ boundary, weight loading, platform.py, npu_ops. The TileLang terms are for the deferred page concepts/tilelang-kernels.

jit-compilation.short: Just-in-time compilation: the program is compiled at run time, at the first call, not when you build the package. TileLang kernel factories compile kernels this way.
jit-compilation.long: DeepInfer can keep the compiled kernels on disk: with DEEPINFER_JIT_CACHE_DIR set, the worker sets TILELANG_CACHE_DIR ({{cite deepinfer/worker/runtime_config.py:45-51}}).

interface-file.short: A Python file directly in tilelang_ops/. It checks the tensors, calls the kernel factory through ops, and also holds a PyTorch reference and the kernel tests.

reference-implementation.short: A slow but simple PyTorch version of a kernel (a function named ..._ref). The kernel tests compare the kernel output with it.

persistent-kernel.short: A kernel that starts one program per core. Each program then loops over many tiles of work, so the number of programs does not depend on the input size.
persistent-kernel.long: Most Ascend factories in DeepInfer use T.Persistent over tile_kernels.get_num_vec_cores() programs ({{cite deepinfer/model_executor/layers/tilelang_ops/asc/swa_index.py:14-35}}).

vector-core.short: A compute unit of an Ascend NPU that does vector (element-wise) work. The Ascend kernels of DeepInfer start one program per vector core.

unified-buffer.short: The small on-chip memory of an Ascend vector core. A kernel copies a tile from device memory into the UB, computes on it, and copies the result back.
unified-buffer.long: A comment in the code calls it shared memory and says that it must be 32-byte aligned ({{cite deepinfer/model_executor/layers/tilelang_ops/asc/compute_seqlens_k_zos.py:21}}).

pdl.short: Programmatic dependent launch: a CUDA feature that lets a kernel start before the kernel before it in the stream ends. The kernel waits at a sync point before it reads earlier results.
pdl.long: Most CUDA kernel files call T.pdl_sync() before the first read, and the worker turns PDL on for tile_kernels on GPU ({{cite deepinfer/worker/runtime_config.py:64-66}}).

safetensors.short: A file format for tensors: an 8-byte header length, a JSON header with the dtype, shape and byte range of each tensor, then the raw bytes.

hf-checkpoint.short: A model folder in the Hugging Face layout: config.json, an index file model.safetensors.index.json, and the weight files (shards) that the index names.

checkpoint-shard.short: One .safetensors file of a checkpoint. A large model is split into many shards; the index file tells which shard holds each tensor.

weight-coverage.short: DeepInfer's plan (HFCoverage) that maps each model parameter to the checkpoint tensors that fill it. A parameter with no source stops the load. An unused checkpoint tensor is ignored.
weight-coverage.long: The check is one-way: load_hf_checkpoint raises only for model parameters that the plan does not cover ({{cite deepinfer/model_executor/model_loader.py:147-149}}).

meta-device.short: A PyTorch device for tensors that have a shape and a dtype but no memory. DeepInfer builds the model there first, then gives each parameter real memory.

attrdict.short: DeepInfer's dict class that also allows attribute access (cfg.moe.n_routed_experts). The + operator merges two of them recursively.

tied-parameter.short: A parameter that shares its storage with another parameter. In DeepInfer, the MTP layers share the embedding and the output head with the main model.

mutex.short: A lock that only one thread can hold at a time. Other threads that want it wait until the holder releases it.

ipc-handle.short: A small block of bytes that lets another process open the same device memory. DeepInfer exports one with cuda_utils.export_ipc_tensor and opens it with import_ipc_tensor.

platform-tag.short: The name <accelerator>-<arch> (for example nvidia-x86_64). The build links the compiled .so files into deepinfer/_so/<tag>/, and the package imports from that folder.

borrowed-view.short: A NumPy array or tensor that points at memory that C++ owns. Python gets no copy. The data is valid only until C++ uses that memory again.
borrowed-view.long: Example: SchedulerOutputs.clone_blocks points into a scheduler vector that the next schedule() clears ({{cite csrc/engine/pybind_scheduler.cpp:41-50}}).

model-metadata.short: A Python class that turns model_cfg.gpt into flat per-layer lists (compress ratio, top-k, SWA, indexer) and checks the supported layouts. Many parts make their own copy.

hf-name-map.short: The rules in hugging_face/names.py that turn a checkpoint tensor name (layers.3.attn.wq_a.weight) into a parameter path of the model (module.module.4.self_attn.Wq.A.weight).
